name: Factor V Leiden
description: Factor V Leiden mutation causes activated protein C resistance, significantly increasing risk of venous thromboembolism (DVT and pulmonary embolism). Heterozygous carriers have 5-10x increased risk; homozygous have 50-100x.

name: Prothrombin G20210A
description: Prothrombin gene mutation leads to elevated prothrombin levels and 2-5x increased risk of venous thromboembolism.

name: APOE e4 determinant (C112R)
description: One of two SNPs that define APOE isoforms. The e4 allele (C at rs429358) is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. One e4 copy increases risk ~3x; two copies increase risk ~12x.

name: APOE e2 determinant (R158C)
description: Second SNP defining APOE isoforms. The e2 allele (T at rs7412) is associated with reduced Alzheimer's risk but increased risk of type III hyperlipoproteinemia.

name: MTHFR C677T
description: Common variant reducing MTHFR enzyme activity. TT genotype has ~30% residual enzyme activity and mildly elevated homocysteine. Clinical significance is often overstated; adequate folate intake usually compensates.

name: Hereditary hemochromatosis (C282Y)
description: Primary mutation causing hereditary hemochromatosis (iron overload). Homozygous C282Y individuals have high penetrance for iron overload, especially males.

name: Type 2 diabetes risk variant
description: The strongest common genetic risk factor for type 2 diabetes. T allele carriers have impaired insulin secretion and ~1.4x increased diabetes risk per allele.

name: FTO obesity risk variant
description: The most studied obesity-associated variant. Each A allele associated with ~1.2 kg higher body weight and 1.3x increased obesity risk.

name: CYP2C9*2 (warfarin metabolism)
description: CYP2C9*2 allele reduces warfarin metabolism to ~12% of wild-type activity. Carriers require lower warfarin doses to avoid bleeding complications.

name: CYP2C9*3 (warfarin metabolism)
description: CYP2C9*3 allele reduces warfarin metabolism to ~5% of wild-type activity. Stronger effect than *2; carriers need significantly lower warfarin doses.

name: CYP2C19*2 (clopidogrel metabolism)
description: Most common CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele. Carriers have reduced activation of clopidogrel, leading to decreased antiplatelet effect and higher cardiovascular risk.

name: SLCO1B1*5 (statin myopathy risk)
description: SLCO1B1 variant reducing hepatic statin uptake. C allele carriers have 4-17x increased risk of simvastatin-induced myopathy.

name: Lactose tolerance/intolerance
description: Primary variant determining lactase persistence in European populations. A allele = lactase persistent (can digest lactose into adulthood). GG genotype = lactase non-persistent (lactose intolerant).

name: Alcohol flush reaction
description: ALDH2 deficiency causing alcohol flush reaction. Common in East Asian populations. A allele carriers accumulate acetaldehyde, causing facial flushing and nausea. Also associated with increased esophageal cancer risk with chronic alcohol use.

name: ACTN3 R577X (muscle fiber type)
description: Determines alpha-actinin-3 expression in fast-twitch muscle fibers. CC = functional protein (sprint/power advantage). TT = no alpha-actinin-3 (may favor endurance). Very common variant with modest athletic effects.

name: COMT Val158Met (stress response)
description: COMT enzyme activity variant. GG (Val/Val) = 'warrior' phenotype with higher stress tolerance but lower cognitive performance under no stress. AA (Met/Met) = 'worrier' phenotype with better cognitive performance but higher stress sensitivity.
